question: Arun travels from City A to City B. If Arun drives his car at (2)/(3)rd of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 38 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Arun would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed becomes 2/3 → Time becomes 3/2 (inverse)

Increase in time = (3/2 − 1) = 1/2 of normal time

Given increase = 38 min

So (1/2) of time = 38 → time = 76 min

**∴ Answer = 76 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduced speed = (2/3) of normal speed, delay = 38 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let normal time = t minutes

⇒ Reduced speed ⇒ new time = (3/2)t

⇒ Increase in time = (3/2)t − t = (1/2)t

⇒ (1/2)t = 38

⇒ t = 76

**∴ The correct answer is 76 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation

Speed and time are inversely proportional.

Speed Reduction Effect

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a.

Time Difference Trick

Extra time = (new time − original time).

Shortcut Insight

Use fractional increase in time directly to avoid equations.
